RANKED COEFFICIENTS OF THE PROVENANCE-FLOOR MODEL
==================================================================

Model: logistic regression (C=1.0, L2) on character n-grams
       of the CDR3 string, ngram_range=(1,4), TF-IDF weighted,
       min_df=3. The peptide was never shown to this model.

Data:      data/TCREpitopePairs.csv
Split:     epitope-disjoint, seed 1
Train:     227,370 pairs
Test:      43,572 pairs, 196 unseen epitopes
Features:  61,665
Test AUROC: 0.7494

A POSITIVE coefficient pushes a sequence toward the label
'binding'. Because the negatives were drawn from a separate
background repertoire, that really means 'toward the positive
source file' rather than toward any binding property.

READ WITH CARE:
  - Features are TF-IDF weighted, so a coefficient is per unit
    of TF-IDF, not per occurrence of the substring.
  - N-grams are nested and correlated (S, SS, SSL all fire
    together), so L2 splits credit among them. Read groups of
    related n-grams as one signal, not as separate findings.
  - Single-feature weights are unstable across seeds even when
    the grouped signal is not. Refit across several seeds and
    keep only what survives before quoting anything.
  - These describe what the model USES, not what causes
    binding. The point is that they are provenance artifacts.
